To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
Chinese lesbians in Mainland China and Hong Kong who experienced more shame were more likely to experience internalized heterosexist beliefs and to have a negative view of their lesbian identity.

(a) shame is a significant predictor of internalized heterosexist attitudes in both samples; (b) internalized heterosexistic attitudes predict lower lesbian identity in both samples; and (c) lesbian identity predicts lower outness in both samples.
shame is associated with a lower likelihood of coming out in both Mainland Chinese and Hong Kong Chinese lesbians, and that this association is mediated by internalized homophobia.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the cultural context of coming out in China.
the role of shame in the coming out process and the relationship between shame, internalized homophobia, and outness among Chinese lesbians in 2 different cultural contexts.
the social construction of shame and its relationship with internalized heterosexist beliefs and the coming-out process.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
shame, as well as the social support of family and friends, plays a significant role in the coming out process of Chinese lesbians.
the more shame the Chinese lesbian has, the more she will be internalized heterosexist, and the less she will value her lesbian identity, and the less likely she is to come out to others.

the more a woman feels shamed for her lesbian identity, the more she will internalize the negative beliefs about her sexual orientation, the less she will value her lesbian identity, and the less likely she is to come out to others.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
coming out to family members and friends in Chinese societies is a difficult and complex process that is related to the internalized shame that is experienced by Chinese lesbians.
coming out to others is related to the degree of one's internalized heterosexist beliefs, which are in turn related to one's level of shame and perceived social support.

the shame that Chinese lesbians experience is a significant factor in the development of internalized heterosexist attitudes, which in turn is associated with a reluctance to disclose one's lesbian identity.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the shame and stigma associated with same-sex orientation are powerful factors that influence lesbian outness and lesbian identity.
shame is a key variable in understanding the coming out experiences of Chinese lesbians.
shame is a significant predictor of lesbian identity development and outness, and that it is important for clinicians and counselors to address shame in their work with Chinese lesbian clients.
